standard.request_selection: omit service_tier and use the normal accounts/fireworks/models/{model_id} model ID
standard.behavior: Default Fireworks Serverless serving path for general use.
standard.pricing: Model-specific Standard prices are in provider_specific.fireworks.serving.standard when normalized.

priority.request_selection: set service_tier=priority on supported OpenAI-compatible chat completions or Anthropic-compatible messages requests
priority.behavior: Higher-reliability path during peak traffic; prioritized above Standard and less likely to be load-shed with 503s.
priority.pricing: Model-specific Priority prices are in provider_specific.fireworks.serving.priority when available.

fast.request_selection: switch the request model ID to the provider-published Fast router ID for supported models
fast.behavior: High-speed serving path for latency-sensitive interactive applications; Fireworks targets 100+ generated tokens/second and says model quality remains the same.
fast.pricing: Model-specific Fast prices and router IDs are in provider_specific.fireworks.serving.fast when available.

fireworks.notes: Fireworks uses provider-native serving path names. Standard is the default base model path with no service_tier parameter. Priority is selected with service_tier=priority on supported base model paths. Fast is represented as separate provider-published router model entries such as accounts/fireworks/routers/kimi-k2p6-fast; it is not the same as Priority.

pricing.notes: Full standard Gemini API token price.

standard.notes: Default Gemini API inference tier when service_tier is omitted.

pricing.notes: Google documents Priority inference as 75–100% more than Standard.

priority.reliability: High, non-sheddable; overflow can gracefully downgrade to Standard.
priority.notes: Swarm fast maps to Google provider-native Priority inference via service_tier=priority.

pricing.notes: Google documents Flex inference as 50% of Standard API pricing.

flex.reliability: Best-effort, sheddable; clients must handle 429/503 and retries.
flex.notes: Flex uses the same service_tier parameter with value flex for latency-tolerant synchronous work.

pricing.notes: Google documents the Gemini Batch API as 50% of Standard API pricing.

batch.latency: Up to 24 hours
batch.reliability: High for throughput
batch.notes: Batch is an asynchronous API surface, not a service_tier value on synchronous requests.

google.notes: Google Gemini thinking controls are model-family dependent: Gemini 3 uses thinkingLevel; Gemini 2.5 uses numeric thinkingBudget. Swarm only exposes exact provider-native settings and does not map Gemini minimal to off because Google says it does not guarantee disabled thinking.

standard.notes: Default OpenAI API serving tier when Priority/Flex is not requested.

priority.notes: Swarm fast maps to OpenAI provider-native Priority processing via service_tier=priority. This is OpenAI API metadata only, not Codex OAuth.

flex.notes: OpenAI Flex processing for latency-tolerant synchronous API requests via service_tier=flex.

batch.notes: OpenAI Batch API pricing; this is an asynchronous API surface, not a service_tier value on synchronous requests.

openai.notes: For OpenAI API only: Swarm fast maps to provider service_tier=priority. Codex OAuth serving remains separate.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter's public Models API exposes base model pricing but does not expose service-tier-specific pricing.

default.notes: Default OpenRouter routing when service_tier is omitted. OpenRouter may normalize upstream base-tier labels, such as Google standard, to default in responses.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents priority as faster and higher cost, but does not expose per-model priority availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

priority.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=priority, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents flex as lower cost and higher latency, but does not expose per-model flex availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

flex.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=flex, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

service_tiers.notes: OpenRouter service_tier is documented as a router-level request parameter with priority/flex values, but /api/v1/models does not list service_tier in supported_parameters and does not publish per-model tier availability or tier pricing. Swarm therefore records this metadata as disabled/unmapped and does not add service_tier to OpenRouter model supported_parameters.

openrouter.notes: OpenRouter accepts router-level service_tier=priority|flex, but Swarm leaves OpenRouter fast/flex disabled because /api/v1/models does not expose reliable per-model tier support or pricing. OpenRouter reasoning controls use the normalized reasoning request object where /api/v1/models advertises reasoning support.

models.description: Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 is a frontier-scale large language model (LLM) trained by NVIDIA, designed to deliver strong agentic, reasoning, and conversational capabilities. It is optimized for the most demanding workloads, including complex multi-step agents, long-context analysis, and high-accuracy reasoning over code, math, and science. The model employs a hybrid Latent Mixture-of-Experts (LatentMoE) architecture, utilizing interleaved Mamba-2 and MoE layers, along with select Attention layers. Like the Super model, the Ultra model incorporates Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) layers for faster text generation and improved quality, and it is trained using an NVFP4 pre-training recipe to maximize compute efficiency. The model has 55B active parameters and 550B parameters in total.

swarm_setting_mappings.notes: OpenRouter documents reasoning.effort=none as disabling reasoning entirely.

thinking.notes: OpenRouter exposes a normalized reasoning request object. Swarm maps effort presets through reasoning.effort and records reasoning.max_tokens as budget-token capable, but does not infer model-specific defaults from the router docs. reasoning.exclude/include_reasoning controls response visibility, not reasoning strength; some reasoning models may not return reasoning content.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter's public Models API exposes base model pricing but does not expose service-tier-specific pricing.

default.notes: Default OpenRouter routing when service_tier is omitted. OpenRouter may normalize upstream base-tier labels, such as Google standard, to default in responses.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents priority as faster and higher cost, but does not expose per-model priority availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

priority.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=priority, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents flex as lower cost and higher latency, but does not expose per-model flex availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

flex.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=flex, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

serving.notes: OpenRouter service_tier is documented as a router-level request parameter with priority/flex values, but /api/v1/models does not list service_tier in supported_parameters and does not publish per-model tier availability or tier pricing. Swarm therefore records this metadata as disabled/unmapped and does not add service_tier to OpenRouter model supported_parameters.

reasoning.note: OpenRouter exposes a normalized reasoning request object. Swarm maps effort presets through reasoning.effort and records reasoning.max_tokens as budget-token capable, but does not infer model-specific defaults from the router docs. reasoning.exclude/include_reasoning controls response visibility, not reasoning strength; some reasoning models may not return reasoning content.

openrouter.note: OpenRouter accepts router-level service_tier=priority|flex, but /api/v1/models does not expose reliable per-model service-tier support or pricing; Swarm does not map fast/flex for OpenRouter models. OpenRouter reasoning controls are documented as a normalized router-level reasoning object, with model-specific supported parameters supplied by /api/v1/models.

default.notes: Default OpenRouter routing when service_tier is omitted. OpenRouter may normalize upstream base-tier labels, such as Google standard, to default in responses.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents priority as faster and higher cost, but does not expose per-model priority availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

priority.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=priority, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

pricing.notes: OpenRouter documents flex as lower cost and higher latency, but does not expose per-model flex availability or pricing in /api/v1/models.

flex.notes: Disabled for Swarm mapping: OpenRouter accepts service_tier=flex, but the public catalog does not confirm which model/provider routes support it.

serving.notes: OpenRouter service_tier is documented as a router-level request parameter with priority/flex values, but /api/v1/models does not list service_tier in supported_parameters and does not publish per-model tier availability or tier pricing. Swarm therefore records this metadata as disabled/unmapped and does not add service_tier to OpenRouter model supported_parameters.

reasoning.note: OpenRouter exposes a normalized reasoning request object. Swarm maps effort presets through reasoning.effort and records reasoning.max_tokens as budget-token capable, but does not infer model-specific defaults from the router docs. reasoning.exclude/include_reasoning controls response visibility, not reasoning strength; some reasoning models may not return reasoning content.

openrouter.note: OpenRouter accepts router-level service_tier=priority|flex, but /api/v1/models does not expose reliable per-model service-tier support or pricing; Swarm does not map fast/flex for OpenRouter models. OpenRouter reasoning controls are documented as a normalized router-level reasoning object, with model-specific supported parameters supplied by /api/v1/models.
